title: conversation-latency-thrift-benchmark-lattice
content:
TL;DR: quick hands-on benchmark comparing three serving variants (base-fp16, q8-fast, q4-hybrid) across conversation lengths and burst patterns. Goal: find low-cost operating points that keep p95 latency under 300ms for short-turn chat (<=512 tokens) while identifying where KV-cache and prefetching buy the most. This is a working notebook-style writeup — experimental notes + ascii charts + actionable hypotheses.

Test matrix and setup:
- Workload: conversational chat mimic (user prompt 30–60 tokens, assistant gen 20–300 tokens depending on scenario). Synthetic arrival patterns: steady (10 qps), bursty (20s bursts at 80 qps every 5 minutes), microbursts (5s at 250 qps).
- Models/variants tested:
  * base-fp16: full-precision serving (reference)
  * q8-fast: 8-bit quant with reduced kernel precision, optimized for throughput
  * q4-hybrid: aggressive 4-bit quant with mixed kernels (prefetch tuned)
- Hardware: single A100 equivalent node type (dedicated pool); same driver/kernel set to avoid infra confounders.
- Config knobs: batch window 8ms (default), dynamic batching on, KV-cache enabled for sessionized runs, prefetch primes at sequence length 128 for predicted continuation.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency (ms) for generation end-to-end (client observed), tokens/sec, cost-per-1k-tokens (estimated from reserved capacity amortized) and observed throughput drop during bursts.

Raw cross-tab (selected rows):
Scenario | Variant    | Seq | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | tokens/s | $/1k toks (est)
Short-turn (<=128) | base-fp16  | 128 | 42      | 165     | 280     | 920      | 0.14
Short-turn (<=128) | q8-fast    | 128 | 35      | 120     | 210     | 1100     | 0.10
Short-turn (<=128) | q4-hybrid  | 128 | 48      | 210     | 420     | 1300     | 0.07
Mid-turn (512)      | base-fp16  | 512 | 110     | 420     | 980     | 360      | 0.15
Mid-turn (512)      | q8-fast    | 512 | 90      | 360     | 720     | 420      | 0.11
Long-turn (2k)      | base-fp16  | 2048| 480     | 2200    | 5200    | 95       | 0.21
Long-turn (2k)      | q8-fast    | 2048| 420     | 1800    | 4100    | 110      | 0.16
Long-turn (2k)      | q4-hybrid  | 2048| 390     | 1500    | 3400    | 140      | 0.12

Quick observations: 
- For short-turn chat, q8-fast dominates for latency and cost — p95 reduced ~28% vs base, tokens/sec improved. q4-hybrid is cheapest per token but p95 suffers due to tail amplification on rare longer generations (likely kernel mismatch + quant noise requiring more attention recomputes).
- Mid-range (512) shows similar pattern but tail sensitivity increases: q4-hybrid p95 penalty grows faster than its cost benefits. That suggests prefetch + hybrid kernels currently insufficient for variance in gen length.
- Long-turns: quantized modes show cost savings but not monotonic latency wins; memory pressure and kv-cache ripples cause p99 amplifications.

Ascii lattice view (qualitative cost vs latency placement):
(Cost axis vertical, lower is better; Latency horizontal, lower is better)
Cost $/1k -->
0.25 |                  ● base-fp16 (long)
0.18 |           ● base-fp16 (mid)         
0.15 |       ● q8-fast (mid)              
0.11 |   ● q8-fast (short)    ● q4-hybrid (long)
0.07 |● q4-hybrid (short)
      ------------------------------- latency -->
      low                            high
(Interpretation: q4-hybrid pushes cost down on average but moves some cases rightwards on latency tail)

Burst behavior notes (microbursts vs steady):
- base-fp16: stable throughput during short bursts up to pre-warmed slot count; p95 spikes when new slots spun up (warmup penalty ~180–350ms depending on concurrency).
- q8-fast: handles bursts better due to faster kernels and smaller memory movement; prewarming reduces spikes to ~90–150ms.
- q4-hybrid: highest throughput, but when cold starts occur the p99 penalty is highest (long tail ~1.5–2x) — indicates load-sensitive compaction/slow path.

KV-cache effect (sessionized runs):
- With KV-cache enabled and high hit rates (>65%): tokens/sec increases 1.6x and cost per 1k down ~20% for q8-fast; p95 moves left by ~40ms for short-turns.
- For q4-hybrid the benefit is similar in avg throughput but tail still worsens on cache misses — cache amplification effect: miss triggers slow path recompute which is more expensive under 4-bit mixed kernels.

Open questions / TO-DOs:
- Re-run with different batch_window settings (8ms vs 12ms vs 20ms) to quantify batching-latency sweet spot for q4-hybrid (hypothesis: slightly larger window reduces tail without much cost increase).
- Need microtrace of kernel-fallback sequences when q4-hybrid hits p99 to confirm compaction/restore path. Add tracing hooks and small repro case.
- Estimate customer-visible cost if shipping q4-hybrid as default for short-turn routes (projected 15–25% cost reduction but risk bump in p99 incidents).
- Compare against multi-node shard (split context across 2 GPUs) for long-turns — might change cost/latency cross-over.

Actionable recommendations (short horizon):
1) Default short-turn routes to q8-fast in Hosted tiers with aggressive KV-cache priming enabled. Rationale: best latency + good cost.
2) Offer q4-hybrid as opt-in "economy" profile with guardrails: per-route p99 alarms + fallback to q8-fast if p99 > 500ms for 5m window.
3) Instrument kernel fallback traces and add a microbench that repros q4-hybrid tail to isolate the slow path.
4) Run batch_window sweep and microburst replay with more seed variance (10 different seeds) then feed into SLO-simulator to quantify incident rate under different routing policies.

Notes to self (drafty):
- Remember to push a short reproducer to PR branch before next sync. Marcus to add the tracing flag in PR #2104.
- Link experiment IDs to ENG-4827 and attach CSVs; record seed and commit SHA for reproducibility.

Appendix: quick reproducibility snippet (pseudo):
- python bench.py --model q8-fast --arrival-profile bursty --seed 422 --kv-cache on --batch-window 8 --out results/q8-bursty-422.csv

End of notebook. This is intentionally compact; follow-up doc should convert selected tables to actual charts and include session-level CDFs for p95/p99 decomposition.

Unresolved: is the long-tail in q4-hybrid primarily IO or compute? kernel-level histograms pending.
